identity.title: Forklift Pre-Shift Inspection Log, Unit FL-2 (Toyota 8FGU25, propane), September 2026, Portland Warehouse
identity.site: Portland — 4410 NW Front Ave, Portland, Oregon 97210

scan.summary: This is your own daily inspection log for one propane forklift (unit FL-2) at the Portland warehouse for September 2026. The rules require the truck to be checked before each shift and pulled from use if a defect affects safety. The log shows that most working days were checked. It also has missing days, a horn defect with no record of what was done about it, no supervisor sign-off, and no entries after September 18.
scan.freshness_note: The last entry is 2026-09-18, which is 12 days before today (2026-09-30). The log shows no inspections for the weekdays September 21–30. Ask whether a second September sheet exists. If there isn't one, find out whether FL-2 was used without being checked or was out of service.

gaps.title: No entries for Sep 3 and Sep 4 even though the truck ran
gaps.description: There are no inspection entries for Thursday Sep 3 or Friday Sep 4. The hour meter went from 4,819 on Sep 2 to 4,834 on Sep 7. That is about two days of normal use, so the truck appears to have been run on those days without a recorded pre-shift check. The sheet itself points this out.
gaps.fix: Ask the operators and supervisor whether the checks were done but not written down. Record what you find as a dated note on the sheet, and don't backfill ticks. Remind operators that the check comes before every shift the truck is used.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7), adopted in Oregon through Oregon OSHA's Division 2 rules
gaps.locator: Page 1, between the Sep 2 and Sep 7 rows; page 2 footnote
gaps.quote: The hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days.

gaps.title: Horn defect on Sep 9 with no record of repair or removal from service
gaps.description: On Sep 9 the horn was marked defective ('Horn not working'), and the same row shows the truck was operated that day by M.C. The next day the horn is ticked OK. Nothing records whether the truck was taken out of service, who fixed the horn, or when. The horn is a warning device, and the rule says a truck with a safety defect must not be used until it is repaired.
gaps.fix: Find the repair record or work order for the horn and attach it to this log, or add a dated note of what was done. Add a defect follow-up column (out of service Y/N, repaired by, date) to the form.

gaps.title: No entries after Sep 18
gaps.description: The log stops at Sep 18. The weekdays Sep 21 through Sep 30 have no inspection entries on this sheet. The truck may have been used without being checked, or the rest of the month may be on another sheet.
gaps.fix: Find the continuation sheet, or confirm whether FL-2 was used from Sep 21 onward. If it was used, record the missing checks as a finding, not as ticks added after the fact.

gaps.title: Supervisor review not signed
gaps.description: The supervisor review line and its date are blank. Because of this, nobody reviewed the missing days or the horn defect.
gaps.fix: Have the supervisor review the sheet, note the findings above, then sign and date it.
gaps.citation: Your own form's requirement, not a regulation
